name: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP)

conventions.compounding: Annual compounding (post-2014 relaunch); accrued and paid at maturity
conventions.quotedAs: KVP is conventionally quoted by its DOUBLING PERIOD (months for principal to double) rather than a headline annual %; an annualised rate is only explicitly published by DEA/NSI from the 2014 relaunch onward
conventions.tenure: Fixed maturity = current doubling period (115 months as of 2026); premature encashment allowed after 2 years 6 months lock-in, then in 6-month blocks
conventions.depositLimitCurrent: No maximum; min Rs 1,000 in multiples of Rs 100 (denominations of 1000/5000/10000/50000 at relaunch)
conventions.administeredBy: DEA / National Savings Institute; India Post and (since relaunch) authorised banks

currentQuarter.nextAnnouncement: Q3 FY2026-27 (Oct-Dec 2026) not yet announced as of 2026-09-27; expect DEA OM ~2026-09-30.

periods.note: Original KVP. NSI's inception page dates this period from 23-03-1988; PIB's 2014 relaunch release instead states the scheme 'was launched by the Government on 1st April, 1988' -- a primary-source date disagreement, both recorded. Doubling/maturity period: 5 years 6 months. No annualised % published by NSI for this era (KVP was always quoted by doubling period, not APR).
Doubling/maturity period: 6 years 6 months. No % published.
Doubling/maturity period: 7 years 3 months. No % published.
Doubling/maturity period: 7 years 8 months. No % published.

Doubling/maturity period: 8 years 7 months (NSI, primary). The 8.41% annualised figure for the final part of this period is from a secondary compilation (Arthapedia/IES) describing conditions 'in 2011' at closure, not a rate NSI itself tabulates numerically for the full 2003-2011 span -- recorded as secondary-sourced.

SCHEME DISCONTINUED. No new KVP certificates issued 2011-12-01 to 2014-11-17, following the Shyamala Gopinath Committee (report 7 June 2011) recommendation that KVP be discontinued as an easily-transferable bearer-like instrument vulnerable to AML/CFT misuse. Existing certificates continued to earn their contracted rate to maturity.

Relaunched with a 100-month (8y4m) doubling period. NSI's own inception page instead dates the relaunch from 23-09-2014, conflicting with PIB's press release and the Arthapedia/IES narrative both stating the relaunch 'was implemented with effect from 18 November 2014' -- recorded as a primary-source date disagreement.
Doubling period 110 months. Confirmed by India Post SB Order 2016 circular.
Doubling period 115 months. NSI page reads 'TO 31.03.2026'; continuation through Q2 FY2026-27 confirmed by TOI/ET/bankbazaar reporting of 30.06.2026 DEA OM.

gaps: No annualised % is available (from NSI or any source found) for the original KVP era 1988-2003; only the officially published doubling/maturity period is on record. Recorded with rate=null rather than backing out an implied rate, per the no-estimation standard.
Exact original-launch date disputed between primary sources: NSI inception page says 23 March 1988; PIB's 2014 press release says 1 April 1988. Both cited, not resolved.

Relaunch date disputed similarly: NSI says 23 September 2014; PIB press release and IES/Arthapedia narrative say 18 November 2014 (matching the date the Finance Minister and Communications Minister jointly relaunched it, per contemporaneous Hindu BusinessLine coverage). Both cited.
8.41% figure for 2011 (pre-discontinuation) is secondary-sourced only (Arthapedia); no primary numeric confirmation located.
notes: KVP is unusual among these schemes in that its primary published parameter is a doubling/maturity period, not a percentage; percentages shown here from 2014 onward are DEA/NSI's own published annualised equivalent, used consistently for cross-scheme comparability.
